body: Malta drives on the left side of the road.
Maltese licence plates feature a blue strip on the left, but what makes them stand out is the common use of short plates.
Malta's landscape features slightly hilly, dry agricultural fields and narrow roads. Due to its Mediterranean climate, you'll often see cacti and other dry shrubs.
Extremely common limestone rock walls are a defining feature of the Maltese landscape. Seeing them is often enough to confirm your location is in Malta.
Most buildings in Malta are low-storey with white to beige walls. Buildings made of limestone are also a common sight.
Traditional covered balconies, often painted in bright colours, are a very common feature on Maltese buildings.
The Maltese word for street is 'triq', and you will see it on nearly every street sign.
Bus stops are a frequent sight in Malta and can sometimes provide useful location information.
Similar to the UK and Ireland, Malta uses distinctive double yellow lines to indicate no-parking zones.
English is the primary language used in Malta.
Besides English, the Maltese language is also common. It uses the Latin script with unique letters like Ċ, Ġ, Ħ, and Ż.
On Gozo Island, regular metal guardrails are uncommon; instead, you'll find low stone barriers.
Bus routes with numbers starting with a 3 are found exclusively on Gozo Island.
These distinctive blue signs are unique to the city of Valletta.
A trekker on a white and blue ship provides coverage between the main island and Gozo Island.
